description: xMustard hook client (WS-40c-b). Cursor has no http and no mcp_tool hook type, so every event spawns xmustard-cursor, which posts the event to the daemon and prints the answer. failClosed is false and the client exits non-zero and never 2 on a failure, so a stopped daemon, an unreadable event or a repository outside the token's workspaces costs an unreduced tool result and never the user's tool call. Only updated_mcp_tool_output is replaced, and only for MCP tools: a Cursor built-in (Shell, Read, Grep, Write, Task) is observed and left as Cursor produced it. preToolUse is registered for Shell alone, because updated_input is documented on the generic hook but is reported to be discarded outside Write and Task.
